fields.title: Polka: question from client security team
fields.summary: The chain's security team asks where requests to the AI assistant go.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we answer and what do we do? Name the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are the Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional local grocery delivery service: 900 partner stores, buyer app, and partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are the Polka product manager. Severny chain asks a question before signing: "Where do customer requests to your AI assistant go, and are they used to train third-party models?" They need the answer this week.
fields.brief/objective: Answer in a way that closes the question while clearing up what will surface in the next audit.
fields.brief/constraints: The answer is needed this week. Own inference takes a quarter and starts at 260 thousand per month.
fields.brief/task: Decide what to answer and what to do before answering.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Data questions are answered with settings, not letters
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Before describing the current state, check what you can close in an hour: zero-retention mode, disabled training, agreed region. And create a subprocessor list — you will be asked for it in the next audit regardless of this deal. Radical answers like own inference or disabling the feature usually solve the wrong problem and cost incomparably more.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Data training is disabled. 30-day retention for abuse monitoring. Processing region agreed. Zero-retention mode is available, not enabled.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Question text, item descriptions, past purchase categories. Name, phone, address, and user ID are not sent.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: DPA with the provider signed. The provider is not listed in the public subprocessor list — there is no list.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: "Zero retention can be enabled via settings, an hour of work. Own inference takes a quarter and starts at 260k/month."
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Answer as is, attaching the DPA
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Zero work. Send the current provider contract and a description of exactly what goes out in the request.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: the answer is honest. 30-day retention may raise additional questions. The lack of a public subprocessor list is a vulnerable spot in any audit.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Enable zero retention, publish the subprocessor list, answer
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Enable zero retention, publish the subprocessor list, answer. One week.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: closes the question completely. An hour of technical work plus legal documents that are needed anyway. The precedent with Domashny confirms sufficiency.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Offer own inference for the enterprise segment
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Offer own inference for the enterprise segment. A quarter, from 260k/month.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: maximum control. Will not make it in time for signing. Economically unjustified for the current number of corporate clients.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Disable the AI assistant for shoppers of this chain
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Disable the AI assistant for shoppers of this chain. One week.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: radically removes the question. Different product quality for different stores, and this is noticeable to buyers who did not choose it.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not know the fate of sent data
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not calculate the economics of own hosting
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not fix processing conditions in the spec
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Boundaries of what can be sent to the model are not fixed
fields.rubric/remediation/4/gap: Does not consider when own inference pays off and when it does not
